+    with Path(path).open("rb") as fh:
+        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)
+    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: spec must be a YAML mapping")
+    for key in ("id", "name"):
+        if not raw.get(key):
+            raise ValueError(f"{path}: spec missing required key '{key}'")
+
+    sections = tuple(
+        RequiredSection(name=s["name"], aliases=tuple(s["aliases"]))
+        for s in raw.get("required_sections", [])
+    )
+
+    narrative_raw = raw.get("narrative")
+    narrative: NarrativeLimit | None = None
+    if narrative_raw is not None:
+        max_words = narrative_raw.get("max_words")
+        max_pages = narrative_raw.get("max_pages")
+        if max_words is None and max_pages is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{path}: narrative block must set max_words and/or max_pages"
+            )
+        narrative = NarrativeLimit(
+            start_section=narrative_raw.get("start_section"),
+            end_section=narrative_raw.get("end_section"),
+            max_words=max_words,
+            max_pages=max_pages,
+        )
+
+    budget_ceiling = raw.get("budget", {}).get("ceiling_usd") if raw.get("budget") else None
+
+    attachments = tuple(
+        RequiredAttachment(name=a["name"], signals=tuple(a["signals"]))
+        for a in raw.get("required_attachments", [])
+    )
+
+    return SolicitationSpec(
+        id=raw["id"],
+        name=raw["name"],
+        required_sections=sections,
+        narrative=narrative,
+        budget_ceiling_usd=budget_ceiling,
+        required_attachments=attachments,
+    )
+
+
+def resolve_spec(solicitation: str | None) -> SolicitationSpec | None:
+    """Resolve CheckContext.solicitation into a spec, or None if unset/not
+    found. Only a genuinely broken YAML file (found but malformed) raises;
+    "no spec given" and "nothing there" are both just None."""
+    if solicitation is None or not solicitation.strip():
+        return None
+    path = Path(solicitation)
+    if not path.is_file() or path.suffix.lower() not in (".yaml", ".yml"):
+        return None
+    return load_spec(path)
+
+
+# --- heading detection ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+_ATX_HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$")
+_FENCE = re.compile(r"^(?:```|~~~)")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class HeadingMatch:
+    level: int
+    title: str
+    start: int
+
+
+def find_headings(text: str) -> list[HeadingMatch]:
+    headings: list[HeadingMatch] = []
+    offset = 0
+    in_fence = False
+    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
+        if _FENCE.match(line):
+            in_fence = not in_fence
+        elif not in_fence:
+            match = _ATX_HEADING.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
+            if match:
+                headings.append(
+                    HeadingMatch(level=len(match.group(1)), title=match.group(2), start=offset)
+                )
+        offset += len(line)
+    return headings
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=2048)
+def _phrase_re(phrase: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
+    return re.compile(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9]){re.escape(phrase)}(?![A-Za-z0-9])", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+
+def section_present(headings: list[HeadingMatch], section: RequiredSection) -> HeadingMatch | None:
+    for heading in headings:
+        if any(_phrase_re(alias).search(heading.title) for alias in section.aliases):
+            return heading
+    return None
+
+
+def attachment_mentioned(text: str, attachment: RequiredAttachment) -> bool:
+    return any(_phrase_re(signal).search(text) for signal in attachment.signals)
+
+
+# --- narrative span / word count ----------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _section_end(headings: list[HeadingMatch], heading: HeadingMatch, text_len: int) -> int:
+    for other in headings:
+        if other.start > heading.start and other.level <= heading.level:
+            return other.start
+    return text_len
+
+
+def _narrative_span(
+    doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], limit: NarrativeLimit
+) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    if limit.start_section is None or limit.end_section is None:
+        return None
+    start_alias_section = RequiredSection(name="", aliases=(limit.start_section,))
+    end_alias_section = RequiredSection(name="", aliases=(limit.end_section,))
+    start_heading = section_present(headings, start_alias_section)
+    end_heading = section_present(headings, end_alias_section)
+    if start_heading is None or end_heading is None:
+        return None
+    end = _section_end(headings, end_heading, len(doc.text))
+    return start_heading.start, end
+
+
+# --- budget total extraction ----------------------------------------------------
+
+_BUDGET_TABLE_ROW = re.compile(
+    r"\|\s*\*{0,2}total\*{0,2}\s*\|\s*\*{0,2}\$\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)\*{0,2}\s*\|",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+_BUDGET_PHRASE = re.compile(
+    r"\btotal\b[^\n$]{0,40}?\$\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class BudgetMatch:
+    amount: float
+    quote: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+
+def find_budget_total(text: str) -> BudgetMatch | None:
+    matches = [*_BUDGET_TABLE_ROW.finditer(text), *_BUDGET_PHRASE.finditer(text)]
+    if not matches:
+        return None
+    m = max(matches, key=lambda m: m.start())
+    amount = float(m.group(1).replace(",", ""))
+    return BudgetMatch(amount=amount, quote=m.group(0), start=m.start(), end=m.end())
+
+
+# --- the registered check ------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _slug(name: str) -> str:
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", name.lower()).strip("-")
+
+
+def _missing_finding(id_prefix: str, label: str, key: str, name: str, spec_id: str) -> Finding:
+    return Finding(
+        id=f"{id_prefix}-{_slug(name)}",
+        label=label,
+        anchor=None,
+        evidence={key: name, "spec_id": spec_id},
+        note=f"required {label.lower()} not found: {name}",
+    )
+
+
+def _check_sections(doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    if not spec.required_sections:
+        return None, []
+    missing = [s.name for s in spec.required_sections if section_present(headings, s) is None]
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_sections",
+        label="Required sections present",
+        result=not missing,
+        detail="all present" if not missing else f"missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
+    )
+    findings = [
+        _missing_finding("compliance-section-missing", "Required section", "section", name, spec.id)
+        for name in missing
+    ]
+    return row, findings
+
+
+def _check_narrative_length(doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    limit = spec.narrative
+    if limit is None:
+        return None
+    span = _narrative_span(doc, headings, limit)
+    if span is None:
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            status="skipped",
+            reason=(
+                f"could not locate '{limit.start_section}'..'{limit.end_section}' "
+                "section boundaries in the document"
+            ),
+        )
+    start, end = span
+    narrative_text = doc.text[start:end]
+    if limit.max_words is not None:
+        count = len(narrative_text.split())
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            result=count <= limit.max_words,
+            detail=f"{count} words (limit {limit.max_words})",
+        )
+    if limit.max_pages is not None:
+        if doc.pages is None:
+            return LedgerRow(
+                check="compliance_narrative_length",
+                label="Narrative length",
+                status="skipped",
+                reason=(
+                    "document has no page count (non-PDF source); configure "
+                    "narrative.max_words to check text-based formats"
+                ),
+            )
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            result=doc.pages <= limit.max_pages,
+            detail=f"{doc.pages} pages (limit {limit.max_pages})",
+        )
+    return None
+
+
+def _check_budget(doc: FlattenedDoc, spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    ceiling = spec.budget_ceiling_usd
+    if ceiling is None:
+        return None, []
+    match = find_budget_total(doc.text)
+    if match is None:
+        row = LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_budget",
+            label="Budget within ceiling",
+            status="skipped",
+            reason="could not find a totalled dollar amount in the document text",
+        )
+        return row, []
+    within = match.amount <= ceiling
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_budget",
+        label="Budget within ceiling",
+        result=within,
+        detail=f"${match.amount:,.0f} vs ${ceiling:,.0f} ceiling",
+    )
+    findings = []
+    if not within:
+        findings.append(
+            Finding(
+                id="compliance-budget-over-ceiling",
+                label="Budget",
+                anchor=Anchor(quote=match.quote, span=Span(start=match.start, end=match.end)),
+                evidence={
+                    "total_usd": match.amount,
+                    "ceiling_usd": ceiling,
+                    "spec_id": spec.id,
+                },
+                note=f"budget total ${match.amount:,.0f} exceeds the ${ceiling:,.0f} ceiling",
+            )
+        )
+    return row, findings
+
+
+def _check_attachments(doc: FlattenedDoc, spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    if not spec.required_attachments:
+        return None, []
+    missing = [a.name for a in spec.required_attachments if not attachment_mentioned(doc.text, a)]
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_attachments",
+        label="Required attachments mentioned",
+        result=not missing,
+        detail="all mentioned" if not missing else f"missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
+    )
+    findings = [
+        _missing_finding(
+            "compliance-attachment-missing", "Required attachment", "attachment", name, spec.id
+        )
+        for name in missing
+    ]
+    return row, findings
+
+
+@register(
+    id="solicitation_compliance",
+    name="Solicitation compliance",
+    tier="deterministic",
+    timeout_s=10.0,
+    applies_to=lambda doc: doc.media_type == "text/markdown",
+)
+def solicitation_compliance(doc: FlattenedDoc, ctx: CheckContext) -> CheckOutput:
+    spec = resolve_spec(ctx.solicitation)
+    if spec is None:
+        given = ctx.solicitation
+        reason = (
+            "no solicitation spec given (--solicitation <path-to-yaml>)"
+            if not given or not given.strip()
+            else f"solicitation spec not found: {given!r}"
+        )
+        return CheckOutput(
+            ledger=[
+                LedgerRow(
+                    check="compliance",
+                    label="Solicitation compliance",
+                    status="skipped",
+                    reason=reason,
+                )
+            ]
+        )
+
+    headings = find_headings(doc.text)
+    ledger: list[LedgerRow] = []
+    findings: list[Finding] = []
+
+    sections_row, sections_findings = _check_sections(doc, headings, spec)
+    if sections_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(sections_row)
+        findings.extend(sections_findings)
+
+    length_row = _check_narrative_length(doc, headings, spec)
+    if length_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(length_row)
+
+    budget_row, budget_findings = _check_budget(doc, spec)
+    if budget_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(budget_row)
+        findings.extend(budget_findings)
+
+    attachments_row, attachments_findings = _check_attachments(doc, spec)
+    if attachments_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(attachments_row)
+        findings.extend(attachments_findings)
+
+    return CheckOutput(ledger=ledger, findings=findings)

+class RequiredSection:
+    name: str
+    aliases: tuple[str, ...]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class RequiredAttachment:
+    name: str
+    signals: tuple[str, ...]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class NarrativeLimit:
+    start_section: str | None
+    end_section: str | None
+    max_words: int | None
+    max_pages: int | None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SolicitationSpec:
+    id: str
+    name: str
+    required_sections: tuple[RequiredSection, ...]
+    narrative: NarrativeLimit | None
+    budget_ceiling_usd: float | None
+    required_attachments: tuple[RequiredAttachment, ...]
+
+
+def load_spec(path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> SolicitationSpec:
+    """Parse+validate a YAML spec file. A spec is a contract: a malformed or
+    incomplete shape raises ValueError rather than silently dropping a field."""
+    with Path(path).open("rb") as fh:
+        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)
+    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: spec must be a YAML mapping")
+    for key in ("id", "name"):
+        if not raw.get(key):
+            raise ValueError(f"{path}: spec missing required key '{key}'")
+
+    sections = tuple(
+        RequiredSection(name=s["name"], aliases=tuple(s["aliases"]))
+        for s in raw.get("required_sections", [])
+    )
+
+    narrative_raw = raw.get("narrative")
+    narrative: NarrativeLimit | None = None
+    if narrative_raw is not None:
+        max_words = narrative_raw.get("max_words")
+        max_pages = narrative_raw.get("max_pages")
+        if max_words is None and max_pages is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{path}: narrative block must set max_words and/or max_pages"
+            )
+        narrative = NarrativeLimit(
+            start_section=narrative_raw.get("start_section"),
+            end_section=narrative_raw.get("end_section"),
+            max_words=max_words,
+            max_pages=max_pages,
+        )
+
+    budget_ceiling = raw.get("budget", {}).get("ceiling_usd") if raw.get("budget") else None
+
+    attachments = tuple(
+        RequiredAttachment(name=a["name"], signals=tuple(a["signals"]))
+        for a in raw.get("required_attachments", [])
+    )
+
+    return SolicitationSpec(
+        id=raw["id"],
+        name=raw["name"],
+        required_sections=sections,
+        narrative=narrative,
+        budget_ceiling_usd=budget_ceiling,
+        required_attachments=attachments,
+    )
+
+
+def resolve_spec(solicitation: str | None) -> SolicitationSpec | None:
+    """Resolve CheckContext.solicitation into a spec, or None if unset/not
+    found. Only a genuinely broken YAML file (found but malformed) raises;
+    "no spec given" and "nothing there" are both just None."""
+    if solicitation is None or not solicitation.strip():
+        return None
+    path = Path(solicitation)
+    if not path.is_file() or path.suffix.lower() not in (".yaml", ".yml"):
+        return None
+    return load_spec(path)
+
+
+# --- heading detection ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+_ATX_HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$")
+_FENCE = re.compile(r"^(?:```|~~~)")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class HeadingMatch:
+    level: int
+    title: str
+    start: int
+
+
+def find_headings(text: str) -> list[HeadingMatch]:
+    headings: list[HeadingMatch] = []
+    offset = 0
+    in_fence = False
+    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
+        if _FENCE.match(line):
+            in_fence = not in_fence
+        elif not in_fence:
+            match = _ATX_HEADING.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
+            if match:
+                headings.append(
+                    HeadingMatch(level=len(match.group(1)), title=match.group(2), start=offset)
+                )
+        offset += len(line)
+    return headings
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=2048)
+def _phrase_re(phrase: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
+    return re.compile(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9]){re.escape(phrase)}(?![A-Za-z0-9])", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+
+def section_present(headings: list[HeadingMatch], section: RequiredSection) -> HeadingMatch | None:
+    for heading in headings:
+        if any(_phrase_re(alias).search(heading.title) for alias in section.aliases):
+            return heading
+    return None
+
+
+def attachment_mentioned(text: str, attachment: RequiredAttachment) -> bool:
+    return any(_phrase_re(signal).search(text) for signal in attachment.signals)
+
+
+# --- narrative span / word count ----------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _section_end(headings: list[HeadingMatch], heading: HeadingMatch, text_len: int) -> int:
+    for other in headings:
+        if other.start > heading.start and other.level <= heading.level:
+            return other.start
+    return text_len
+
+
+def _narrative_span(
+    doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], limit: NarrativeLimit
+) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    if limit.start_section is None or limit.end_section is None:
+        return None
+    start_alias_section = RequiredSection(name="", aliases=(limit.start_section,))
+    end_alias_section = RequiredSection(name="", aliases=(limit.end_section,))
+    start_heading = section_present(headings, start_alias_section)
+    end_heading = section_present(headings, end_alias_section)
+    if start_heading is None or end_heading is None:
+        return None
+    end = _section_end(headings, end_heading, len(doc.text))
+    return start_heading.start, end
+
+
+# --- budget total extraction ----------------------------------------------------
+
+_BUDGET_TABLE_ROW = re.compile(
+    r"\|\s*\*{0,2}total\*{0,2}\s*\|\s*\*{0,2}\$\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)\*{0,2}\s*\|",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+_BUDGET_PHRASE = re.compile(
+    r"\btotal\b[^\n$]{0,40}?\$\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class BudgetMatch:
+    amount: float
+    quote: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+
+def find_budget_total(text: str) -> BudgetMatch | None:
+    matches = [*_BUDGET_TABLE_ROW.finditer(text), *_BUDGET_PHRASE.finditer(text)]
+    if not matches:
+        return None
+    m = max(matches, key=lambda m: m.start())
+    amount = float(m.group(1).replace(",", ""))
+    return BudgetMatch(amount=amount, quote=m.group(0), start=m.start(), end=m.end())
+
+
+# --- the registered check ------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _slug(name: str) -> str:
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", name.lower()).strip("-")
+
+
+def _missing_finding(id_prefix: str, label: str, key: str, name: str, spec_id: str) -> Finding:
+    return Finding(
+        id=f"{id_prefix}-{_slug(name)}",
+        label=label,
+        anchor=None,
+        evidence={key: name, "spec_id": spec_id},
+        note=f"required {label.lower()} not found: {name}",
+    )
+
+
+def _check_sections(doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    if not spec.required_sections:
+        return None, []
+    missing = [s.name for s in spec.required_sections if section_present(headings, s) is None]
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_sections",
+        label="Required sections present",
+        result=not missing,
+        detail="all present" if not missing else f"missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
+    )
+    findings = [
+        _missing_finding("compliance-section-missing", "Required section", "section", name, spec.id)
+        for name in missing
+    ]
+    return row, findings
+
+
+def _check_narrative_length(doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    limit = spec.narrative
+    if limit is None:
+        return None
+    span = _narrative_span(doc, headings, limit)
+    if span is None:
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            status="skipped",
+            reason=(
+                f"could not locate '{limit.start_section}'..'{limit.end_section}' "
+                "section boundaries in the document"
+            ),
+        )
+    start, end = span
+    narrative_text = doc.text[start:end]
+    if limit.max_words is not None:
+        count = len(narrative_text.split())
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            result=count <= limit.max_words,
+            detail=f"{count} words (limit {limit.max_words})",
+        )
+    if limit.max_pages is not None:
+        if doc.pages is None:
+            return LedgerRow(
+                check="compliance_narrative_length",
+                label="Narrative length",
+                status="skipped",
+                reason=(
+                    "document has no page count (non-PDF source); configure "
+                    "narrative.max_words to check text-based formats"
+                ),
+            )
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            result=doc.pages <= limit.max_pages,
+            detail=f"{doc.pages} pages (limit {limit.max_pages})",
+        )
+    return None
+
+
+def _check_budget(doc: FlattenedDoc, spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    ceiling = spec.budget_ceiling_usd
+    if ceiling is None:
+        return None, []
+    match = find_budget_total(doc.text)
+    if match is None:
+        row = LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_budget",
+            label="Budget within ceiling",
+            status="skipped",
+            reason="could not find a totalled dollar amount in the document text",
+        )
+        return row, []
+    within = match.amount <= ceiling
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_budget",
+        label="Budget within ceiling",
+        result=within,
+        detail=f"${match.amount:,.0f} vs ${ceiling:,.0f} ceiling",
+    )
+    findings = []
+    if not within:
+        findings.append(
+            Finding(
+                id="compliance-budget-over-ceiling",
+                label="Budget",
+                anchor=Anchor(quote=match.quote, span=Span(start=match.start, end=match.end)),
+                evidence={
+                    "total_usd": match.amount,
+                    "ceiling_usd": ceiling,
+                    "spec_id": spec.id,
+                },
+                note=f"budget total ${match.amount:,.0f} exceeds the ${ceiling:,.0f} ceiling",
+            )
+        )
+    return row, findings
+
+
+def _check_attachments(doc: FlattenedDoc, spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    if not spec.required_attachments:
+        return None, []
+    missing = [a.name for a in spec.required_attachments if not attachment_mentioned(doc.text, a)]
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_attachments",
+        label="Required attachments mentioned",
+        result=not missing,
+        detail="all mentioned" if not missing else f"missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
+    )
+    findings = [
+        _missing_finding(
+            "compliance-attachment-missing", "Required attachment", "attachment", name, spec.id
+        )
+        for name in missing
+    ]
+    return row, findings
+
+
+@register(
+    id="solicitation_compliance",
+    name="Solicitation compliance",
+    tier="deterministic",
+    timeout_s=10.0,
+    applies_to=lambda doc: doc.media_type == "text/markdown",
+)
+def solicitation_compliance(doc: FlattenedDoc, ctx: CheckContext) -> CheckOutput:
+    spec = resolve_spec(ctx.solicitation)
+    if spec is None:
+        given = ctx.solicitation
+        reason = (
+            "no solicitation spec given (--solicitation <path-to-yaml>)"
+            if not given or not given.strip()
+            else f"solicitation spec not found: {given!r}"
+        )
+        return CheckOutput(
+            ledger=[
+                LedgerRow(
+                    check="compliance",
+                    label="Solicitation compliance",
+                    status="skipped",
+                    reason=reason,
+                )
+            ]
+        )
+    return _evaluate(doc, spec)
+
+
+def _evaluate(doc: FlattenedDoc, spec: SolicitationSpec) -> CheckOutput:
+    headings = find_headings(doc.text)
+    ledger: list[LedgerRow] = []
+    findings: list[Finding] = []
+
+    sections_row, sections_findings = _check_sections(doc, headings, spec)
+    if sections_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(sections_row)
+        findings.extend(sections_findings)
+
+    length_row = _check_narrative_length(doc, headings, spec)
+    if length_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(length_row)
+
+    budget_row, budget_findings = _check_budget(doc, spec)
+    if budget_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(budget_row)
+        findings.extend(budget_findings)
+
+    attachments_row, attachments_findings = _check_attachments(doc, spec)
+    if attachments_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(attachments_row)
+        findings.extend(attachments_findings)
+
+    return CheckOutput(ledger=ledger, findings=findings)

+"""Solicitation compliance checks (#16): one YAML spec drives section
+presence, narrative length, budget ceiling, and attachment-mention checks.
+Deterministic tier, no LLM and no network.
+
+Required-section and attachment names are alias-matched against whatever
+headings/text the applicant actually wrote, not the RFP's exact wording — a
+real applicant writes "Aims", not "Specific Aims". Matching is case-insensitive,
+whole-word/phrase (same boundary regex as ``checks/tagging.py``'s
+``_phrase_re``), never naive substring.
+
+This pass only detects ATX (``#``) markdown headings, so the registered check
+is scoped to ``media_type == "text/markdown"`` via ``applies_to`` — a PDF/DOCX
+proposal reports "not applicable to this document" rather than a wrong
+"everything is missing" result. PDF/DOCX heading detection is follow-up work.
+
+Eligibility and priority-area fit (the issue's LLM-judgment tier) are out of
+scope for this pass: no LLM client exists in the codebase yet (#37 is still
+design-only) — see the #16 issue comment for the scoping call.

+import re
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import lru_cache

+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class RequiredSection:
+    name: str
+    aliases: tuple[str, ...]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class RequiredAttachment:
+    name: str
+    signals: tuple[str, ...]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class NarrativeLimit:
+    start_section: str | None
+    end_section: str | None
+    max_words: int | None
+    max_pages: int | None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SolicitationSpec:
+    id: str
+    name: str
+    required_sections: tuple[RequiredSection, ...]
+    narrative: NarrativeLimit | None
+    budget_ceiling_usd: float | None
+    required_attachments: tuple[RequiredAttachment, ...]
+
+
+def load_spec(path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> SolicitationSpec:
+    """Parse+validate a YAML spec file. A spec is a contract: a malformed or
+    incomplete shape raises ValueError rather than silently dropping a field."""
+    with Path(path).open("rb") as fh:
+        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)
+    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: spec must be a YAML mapping")
+    for key in ("id", "name"):
+        if not raw.get(key):
+            raise ValueError(f"{path}: spec missing required key '{key}'")
+
+    sections = tuple(
+        RequiredSection(name=s["name"], aliases=tuple(s["aliases"]))
+        for s in raw.get("required_sections", [])
+    )
+
+    narrative_raw = raw.get("narrative")
+    narrative: NarrativeLimit | None = None
+    if narrative_raw is not None:
+        max_words = narrative_raw.get("max_words")
+        max_pages = narrative_raw.get("max_pages")
+        if max_words is None and max_pages is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{path}: narrative block must set max_words and/or max_pages"
+            )
+        narrative = NarrativeLimit(
+            start_section=narrative_raw.get("start_section"),
+            end_section=narrative_raw.get("end_section"),
+            max_words=max_words,
+            max_pages=max_pages,
+        )
+
+    budget_ceiling = raw.get("budget", {}).get("ceiling_usd") if raw.get("budget") else None
+
+    attachments = tuple(
+        RequiredAttachment(name=a["name"], signals=tuple(a["signals"]))
+        for a in raw.get("required_attachments", [])
+    )
+
+    return SolicitationSpec(
+        id=raw["id"],
+        name=raw["name"],
+        required_sections=sections,
+        narrative=narrative,
+        budget_ceiling_usd=budget_ceiling,
+        required_attachments=attachments,

+
+
+def resolve_spec(solicitation: str | None) -> SolicitationSpec | None:
+    """Resolve CheckContext.solicitation into a spec, or None if unset/not
+    found. Only a genuinely broken YAML file (found but malformed) raises;
+    "no spec given" and "nothing there" are both just None."""
+    if solicitation is None or not solicitation.strip():
+        return None
+    path = Path(solicitation)
+    if not path.is_file() or path.suffix.lower() not in (".yaml", ".yml"):
+        return None

+# --- heading detection ---------------------------------------------------------

+_ATX_HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$")
+_FENCE = re.compile(r"^(?:```|~~~)")

+@dataclass(frozen=True)

+    level: int
+    title: str
+    start: int
+

+def find_headings(text: str) -> list[HeadingMatch]:

+    in_fence = False
+    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
+        if _FENCE.match(line):
+            in_fence = not in_fence
+        elif not in_fence:
+            match = _ATX_HEADING.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
+            if match:
+                headings.append(
+                    HeadingMatch(level=len(match.group(1)), title=match.group(2), start=offset)
+                )
+        offset += len(line)

+@lru_cache(maxsize=2048)
+def _phrase_re(phrase: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
+    return re.compile(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9]){re.escape(phrase)}(?![A-Za-z0-9])", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+
+def section_present(headings: list[HeadingMatch], section: RequiredSection) -> HeadingMatch | None:
+    for heading in headings:
+        if any(_phrase_re(alias).search(heading.title) for alias in section.aliases):
+            return heading
+    return None
+
+

+    return any(_phrase_re(signal).search(text) for signal in attachment.signals)
+
+
+# --- narrative span / word count ----------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _section_end(headings: list[HeadingMatch], heading: HeadingMatch, text_len: int) -> int:
+    for other in headings:
+        if other.start > heading.start and other.level <= heading.level:
+            return other.start
+    return text_len
+
+
+def _narrative_span(
+    doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], limit: NarrativeLimit
+) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    if limit.start_section is None or limit.end_section is None:
+        return None
+    start_alias_section = RequiredSection(name="", aliases=(limit.start_section,))
+    end_alias_section = RequiredSection(name="", aliases=(limit.end_section,))
+    start_heading = section_present(headings, start_alias_section)
+    end_heading = section_present(headings, end_alias_section)
+    if start_heading is None or end_heading is None:
+        return None
+    end = _section_end(headings, end_heading, len(doc.text))

+_BUDGET_PHRASE = re.compile(
+    r"\btotal\b[^\n$]{0,40}?\$\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)",

+    amount: float
+    quote: str
+    start: int
+    end: int

+    m = max(matches, key=lambda m: m.start())

+

+def _slug(name: str) -> str:

+def _check_sections(doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    if not spec.required_sections:
+        return None, []
+    missing = [s.name for s in spec.required_sections if section_present(headings, s) is None]
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_sections",
+        label="Required sections present",
+        result=not missing,
+        detail="all present" if not missing else f"missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
+    )

+            label="Narrative length",

+    missing = [a.name for a in spec.required_attachments if not attachment_mentioned(doc.text, a)]

+"""Solicitation compliance checks (#16): one YAML spec drives section
+presence, narrative length, budget ceiling, and attachment-mention checks.
+Deterministic tier, no LLM and no network.

+Required-section and attachment names are alias-matched against whatever
+headings/text the applicant actually wrote, not the RFP's exact wording — a
+real applicant writes "Aims", not "Specific Aims". Matching is case-insensitive,
+whole-word/phrase (same boundary regex as ``checks/tagging.py``'s
+``_phrase_re``), never naive substring.
+
+This pass only detects ATX (``#``) markdown headings, so the registered check
+is scoped to ``media_type == "text/markdown"`` via ``applies_to`` — a PDF/DOCX
+proposal reports "not applicable to this document" rather than a wrong
+"everything is missing" result. PDF/DOCX heading detection is follow-up work.
+
+Eligibility and priority-area fit (the issue's LLM-judgment tier) are out of
+scope for this pass: no LLM client exists in the codebase yet (#37 is still
+design-only) — see the #16 issue comment for the scoping call.
+"""
+

+
+import os
+import re
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import lru_cache
+from pathlib import Path
+

+        note=f"required {label.lower()} not found: {name}",
+    )
+
+
+def _check_sections(doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    if not spec.required_sections:
+        return None, []
+    missing = [s.name for s in spec.required_sections if section_present(headings, s) is None]
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_sections",
+        label="Required sections present",
+        result=not missing,
+        detail="all present" if not missing else f"missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
+    )
+    findings = [
+        _missing_finding("compliance-section-missing", "Required section", "section", name, spec.id)
+        for name in missing
+    ]
+    return row, findings
+
+
+def _check_narrative_length(
+    doc: FlattenedDoc, headings: list[HeadingMatch], spec: SolicitationSpec
+):
+    limit = spec.narrative
+    if limit is None:
+        return None
+    span = _narrative_span(doc, headings, spec, limit)
+    if span is None:
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            status="skipped",
+            reason=(
+                f"could not locate '{limit.start_section}'..'{limit.end_section}' "
+                "section boundaries in the document"
+            ),
+        )
+    start, end = span
+    narrative_text = doc.text[start:end]
+    if limit.max_words is not None:
+        count = len(narrative_text.split())
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            result=count <= limit.max_words,
+            detail=f"{count} words (limit {limit.max_words})",
+        )
+    if limit.max_pages is not None:
+        if doc.pages is None:
+            return LedgerRow(
+                check="compliance_narrative_length",
+                label="Narrative length",
+                status="skipped",
+                reason=(
+                    "document has no page count (non-PDF source); configure "
+                    "narrative.max_words to check text-based formats"
+                ),
+            )
+        return LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_narrative_length",
+            label="Narrative length",
+            result=doc.pages <= limit.max_pages,
+            detail=f"{doc.pages} pages (limit {limit.max_pages})",
+        )

+    ceiling = spec.budget_ceiling_usd
+    if ceiling is None:
+        return None, []
+    match = find_budget_total(doc.text)
+    if match is None:
+        row = LedgerRow(
+            check="compliance_budget",
+            label="Budget within ceiling",
+            status="skipped",
+            reason="could not find a totalled dollar amount in the document text",
+        )
+        return row, []
+    within = match.amount <= ceiling
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_budget",
+        label="Budget within ceiling",
+        result=within,
+        detail=f"${match.amount:,.0f} vs ${ceiling:,.0f} ceiling",
+    )
+    findings = []
+    if not within:
+        findings.append(
+            Finding(
+                id="compliance-budget-over-ceiling",
+                label="Budget",
+                anchor=Anchor(quote=match.quote, span=Span(start=match.start, end=match.end)),
+                evidence={
+                    "total_usd": match.amount,
+                    "ceiling_usd": ceiling,
+                    "spec_id": spec.id,
+                },
+                note=f"budget total ${match.amount:,.0f} exceeds the ${ceiling:,.0f} ceiling",
+            )
+        )
+    return row, findings

+
+def _check_attachments(doc: FlattenedDoc, spec: SolicitationSpec):
+    if not spec.required_attachments:
+        return None, []
+    missing = [a.name for a in spec.required_attachments if not attachment_mentioned(doc.text, a)]
+    row = LedgerRow(
+        check="compliance_attachments",
+        label="Required attachments mentioned",
+        result=not missing,
+        detail="all mentioned" if not missing else f"missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
+    )
+    findings = [
+        _missing_finding(
+            "compliance-attachment-missing", "Required attachment", "attachment", name, spec.id
+        )
+        for name in missing
+    ]
+    return row, findings

+
+@register(
+    id="solicitation_compliance",
+    name="Solicitation compliance",
+    tier="deterministic",
+    timeout_s=10.0,
+    applies_to=lambda doc: doc.media_type == "text/markdown",

+    spec = resolve_spec(ctx.solicitation)

+        given = ctx.solicitation
+        reason = (
+            "no solicitation spec given (--solicitation <path-to-yaml>)"
+            if not given or not given.strip()
+            else f"solicitation spec not found: {given!r}"
+        )
+        return CheckOutput(
+            ledger=[
+                LedgerRow(
+                    check="compliance",
+                    label="Solicitation compliance",
+                    status="skipped",

+                )
+            ]
+        )

+def _evaluate(doc: FlattenedDoc, spec: SolicitationSpec) -> CheckOutput:

+    findings: list[Finding] = []

+    sections_row, sections_findings = _check_sections(doc, headings, spec)
+    if sections_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(sections_row)
+        findings.extend(sections_findings)
+
+    length_row = _check_narrative_length(doc, headings, spec)
+    if length_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(length_row)
+
+    budget_row, budget_findings = _check_budget(doc, spec)
+    if budget_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(budget_row)
+        findings.extend(budget_findings)
+
+    attachments_row, attachments_findings = _check_attachments(doc, spec)
+    if attachments_row is not None:
+        ledger.append(attachments_row)
+        findings.extend(attachments_findings)
+
+    return CheckOutput(ledger=ledger, findings=findings)

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
#16: solicitation compliance checks (deterministic tier)

YAML-driven checker in slopchecker.checks.compliance: required-section
presence, narrative length (word or page limit), budget-total-vs-ceiling,
and required-attachment mentions. Section/attachment matching is
alias-based against whatever the applicant actually wrote, not the RFP's
exact heading wording. Registered as solicitation_compliance,
tier=deterministic, scoped to text/markdown via applies_to (this pass
only detects ATX headings; PDF/DOCX heading detection is follow-up work).

No spec given, or a --solicitation value that doesn't resolve to a real
YAML file, degrades to a single skipped ledger row rather than an error.
Each dimension a spec doesn't configure is simply absent from the ledger,
not a gap -- a spec with just required_sections runs only that check.

Tested end-to-end against the two real RFPs already in fixtures/rubrics/
(hand-compiled into tests/fixtures/solicitations/*.yaml) and their paired
proposals in harness/fixtures/ -- ground truth hand-verified against the
source RFP text. Confirms both documented planted violations per fixture
plus one undocumented one each (missing Data Management Plan / missing
Evaluation Plan) found by actually reading the proposals rather than
trusting the fixtures README's violation list to be exhaustive.

Scoped out of this pass: the LLM-judgment tier (eligibility/priority-area
fit) from the issue's scope -- no LLM client exists in the codebase yet
(#37 is still design-only). See the #16 issue comment for the full call.

28 new tests, full suite green (503 passed), ruff clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

[project]
name = "slopchecker"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Automating slop checks for funding proposals"
requires-python = ">=3.11"

dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.7",
    "typer>=0.12",
    "rich>=13.7",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Heavy/optional deps live behind extras so someone working on citations
# doesn't need the PDF or LLM stack installed (see #2).
pdf = ["pymupdf>=1.24"]
docx = ["python-docx>=1.1"]
llm = ["anthropic>=0.40"]
# The web layer over the pipeline (#27) — see slopchecker/web.py.
web = ["fastapi>=0.115", "uvicorn>=0.30", "python-multipart>=0.0.9"]
# Validation harness (#29): planted-defect injector + recall report.
harness = ["pyyaml>=6.0"]
# Corpus similarity check (#14): MinHash + LSH for near-duplicate detection.
similarity = ["datasketch>=1.6"]
dev = ["ruff>=0.5", "pytest>=8.2", "mypy>=1.10"]

[project.scripts]
slopcheck = "slopchecker.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

"""Rubric-dependent checks (#90): the submission against the funder's own rules.

First of the family: budget ceiling. Deterministic tier — conservative
pattern-matching over the rubric text and the proposal's budget table, and
every way the extraction can fall short degrades to a skipped gap row with
the reason, never a guess. No rubric on the context is itself a gap
("not checked against a solicitation"), which keeps the coverage story
honest when the caller didn't supply one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from slopchecker.models import Anchor, CheckResult, Finding, FlattenedDoc, LedgerRow, Span
from slopchecker.pipeline.registry import CheckContext, CheckOutput, register

_AMOUNT = re.compile(r"\$\s?(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+|\d+)(?:\.\d+)?")

# Phrases that mark an amount as the award ceiling. Two tiers: "strong"
# wordings are unambiguous caps; "weak" ones ("up to") also appear in
# non-cap contexts, so they only count when no strong line exists.
_STRONG_CAP = re.compile(
    r"(?:may|must|shall|will)?\s*not\s+exceed|no\s+more\s+than|maximum\s+award"
    r"|award\s+ceiling|ceiling|not\s+to\s+exceed|requesting\s+more\s+than",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_WEAK_CAP = re.compile(r"up\s+to|maximum", re.IGNORECASE)

_TOTAL_LINE = re.compile(r"total", re.IGNORECASE)


def _to_number(amount: str) -> float:
    return float(amount.replace(",", ""))


def _find_ceiling(text: str) -> tuple[float, str] | None:
    """The award ceiling stated in rubric text, with the line that states it.

    Returns None when no cap wording is found or when cap lines name more
    than one distinct amount (ambiguous — a gap, not a coin flip).
    """
    strong: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
    weak: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        amounts = _AMOUNT.findall(line)
        if not amounts:
            continue
        if _STRONG_CAP.search(line):
            strong.extend((_to_number(a), line.strip()) for a in amounts)
        elif _WEAK_CAP.search(line):
            weak.extend((_to_number(a), line.strip()) for a in amounts)
    for candidates in (strong, weak):
        values = {v for v, _ in candidates}
        if len(values) == 1:
            return candidates[0]
    return None

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
#16: solicitation compliance checks (deterministic tier)

YAML-driven checker in slopchecker.checks.compliance: required-section
presence, narrative length (word or page limit), budget-total-vs-ceiling,
and required-attachment mentions -- one YAML spec drives all four, so a
new solicitation needs no code (issue AC #1). Section/attachment matching
is alias-based against whatever the applicant actually wrote, not the
RFP's exact heading wording. Registered as solicitation_compliance,
tier=deterministic, scoped to text/markdown via applies_to (this pass
only detects ATX headings; PDF/DOCX heading detection is follow-up work).

No spec given, or a --solicitation value that doesn't resolve to a real
YAML file, degrades to a single skipped ledger row rather than an error.
Each dimension a spec doesn't configure is simply absent from the ledger,
not a gap -- a spec with just required_sections runs only that check.

pyyaml moves from the harness-only extra to a base dependency since the
spec loader needs it at runtime.

Tested end-to-end against the two real RFPs already in fixtures/rubrics/
(hand-compiled into tests/fixtures/solicitations/*.yaml) and their paired
proposals in harness/fixtures/ -- ground truth hand-verified against the
source RFP text, then confirmed live via the CLI. Confirms both
documented planted violations per fixture plus one undocumented one each
(missing Data Management Plan / missing Evaluation Plan) found by
actually reading the proposals.

Overlaps partially with #90's rubric_budget_ceiling (pipeline/checks_rubric.py,
just landed): that check parses a rubric doc's raw prose for a ceiling
phrase at runtime; this one is spec-driven per the issue's AC #1 and
covers three more dimensions it doesn't touch. Noted on the #16 issue
thread rather than silently duplicating -- worth reconciling later, not
blocking either check meanwhile.

Scoped out of this pass: the LLM-judgment tier (eligibility/priority-area
fit) from the issue's scope -- no LLM client exists in the codebase yet
(#37 is still design-only). See the #16 issue comment for the full call.

28 new tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

input.body:
## Summary

- Adds `slopchecker.checks.compliance`: a YAML-spec-driven solicitation compliance checker. One spec drives four checks — required-section presence, narrative length (word or page limit), budget-total-vs-ceiling, required-attachment mentions — so adding a new solicitation needs no code (issue AC #1).
- Section/attachment matching is alias-based against whatever the applicant actually wrote (e.g. "Aims" for "Specific Aims"), not the RFP's exact heading wording — same whole-word/phrase boundary matching as `checks/tagging.py`.
- Registered as `solicitation_compliance`, `tier=deterministic`, scoped to `text/markdown` via `applies_to` — this pass only detects ATX (`#`) headings, so it reports "not applicable" rather than a wrong "everything missing" result on a PDF/DOCX proposal. PDF/DOCX heading detection is follow-up work.
- No `--solicitation` given, or a value that doesn't resolve to a real YAML file, degrades to one `skipped` ledger row rather than an error. A spec dimension left unconfigured (e.g. no `required_attachments`) is simply absent from the ledger, not a gap.
- Moves `pyyaml` from the `harness`-only extra to a base dependency (the spec loader needs it at runtime).
- Two hand-compiled YAML specs (`tests/fixtures/solicitations/{aldergrove-cca,hartwell-eig}.yaml`) transcribed from the real RFPs in `fixtures/rubrics/`, tested end-to-end against their paired proposals in `harness/fixtures/`. Ground truth was hand-verified against the source RFP text, then confirmed live via the CLI — both fixtures reproduce their documented planted violations, plus one undocumented one each (missing "Data Management Plan" / missing "Evaluation Plan") found by actually reading the proposals rather than trusting the fixtures README's violation list to be exhaustive.

## Known overlap (flagged, not resolved here)

`pipeline/checks_rubric.py`'s `rubric_budget_ceiling` (#90, just landed in `debb439`) also checks budget-vs-ceiling, but via a different mechanism — it regex-parses a rubric document's raw prose for a cap phrase at runtime, no YAML spec involved. Per Emerson's own STATUS.md entry that check is an intentional stepping stone toward #16 ("next: web rubric upload slot, then spec-drafting bridge to #16"), not a competing final design. This PR is the spec-driven design the issue's AC #1 actually asks for, and covers three dimensions `rubric_budget_ceiling` doesn't touch. Leaving the two to coexist for now and flagging reconciliation as a follow-up on the issue thread rather than blocking on it.

## Scoped out of this pass

The LLM-judgment tier (eligibility fit, priority-area fit) from the issue's scope — no LLM client exists in the codebase yet (#37 is still design-only), and stubbing one out would be scope creep into that ticket. Also skipping the optional "LLM drafts a spec from a PDF" bullet, explicitly optional in the issue.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest -q` — 591 passed
- [x] `ruff check` clean on new files
- [x] End-to-end CLI smoke test against both real fixture pairs (`slopcheck run ... --solicitation ...`), output matches hand-verified ground truth
- [x] Verified a quote-anchored budget finding renders correctly in `report.json`

## What's new

Grant budgets are now **itemized** (personnel / equipment / travel / indirect + a stated total). New grant-only slop defect **`budget_math`**: the stated total does not equal the sum of the line items.

Unlike wrong-paper and near-duplicate, this one is **deterministically checkable** — sum the line items, compare to the total. `score.py` scores it with a label-aware check (robust to the sentence-shuffle in laundered docs) and the naive baseline nails it: **precision/recall 1.00**.

| defect | naive recall | requires |
|---|---|---|
| `has_fabricated_citations` | 1.00 | DOI resolution |

| `missing_methods` | 1.00 | text heuristic |
| `has_mismatched_citations` | **0.00** | resolution + metadata compare |
| `is_near_duplicate` | **0.00** | corpus-wide similarity |

Confined to `src/slopchecker/report/` (mine per the ownership table) and its generated output. No `worker/src/`, no `wrangler.toml`.

## It's a value swap, not a restructure

`report.css` consumes exactly the twelve colour tokens the new palette already defines, under the same names. So this changes values in the `:root` blocks and leaves every consuming rule untouched.

## The swap alone would have hidden a real bug

`.a-id` — the annotation ID badges — hardcoded `color: #fff` against `--no` / `--yes` / `--score` / `--soft` fills. Those tokens invert to light pastels in dark mode, so it was white-on-pastel:

| dark mode | `#fff` before | `var(--on-strong)` after |
|---|---|---|
| on `--no` `#E3796F` | 2.90 | **6.26** |
| on `--yes` `#6DC194` | 2.16 | **8.41** |
| on `--score` `#9BA9EC` | 2.26 | **8.04** |
| on `--soft` `#9BABBC` | 2.35 | **7.75** |

@etbrooking — this is the same defect you fixed on the landing page in #106 ("buttons and chip badges hardcoded `#fff` over inverted light fills"). It existed identically here, and a straight palette swap would have carried it forward looking fine in light mode. Fixed the same way you did, with an `--on-strong` that flips to near-black in dark mode. Every colour in `report.css` now goes through a token — no hardcoded values left.

## Also clears both light-mode AA failures from the earlier audit

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `--soft` on `--panel` | 4.32 ❌ | **5.13** |
| `--yes` on `--panel` | 4.49 ❌ | **4.94** |

Everything else clears comfortably (`ink on bg` 15.65, `accent on bg` 7.62). `--rule` on `--bg` is 1.31, but that token is only used for dividers, which are decorative rather than UI-component boundaries — noted in the ai-log so nobody re-flags it. (#26)

## `data-theme` question is settled

The audit flagged `:root[data-theme="light"|"dark"]` as dead CSS — nothing ever set the attribute. #106 dropped those blocks from `index.html` entirely, which answers it by precedent, so they're deleted here too. Zero `data-theme` references remain in the repo.

## One copy correction

The legend read "purple = detector score". `--score` is now `#4A5CA6`, an indigo. Changed in `html.py` — leaving it would have shipped a statement that's simply false about what's on screen.

## Verification

- `demo-report.html` regenerated via `slopcheck render`, never hand-edited — and regenerated again after rebasing onto current main, byte-identical, so it isn't stale.
- Full suite: **473 passed, 1 skipped, 9 deselected**.
- Rendered and inspected in the browser at 1280px; computed `--accent` reads `#14568F`, badges render, rail intact.

## Two things worth knowing

- **Regenerating needs Python 3.11+.** This machine had only system 3.9.6, which dies on `zip(strict=True)` in the renderer. I installed `python@3.11` and made a gitignored `.venv`. Command is `slopcheck render tests/fixtures/sample_report.json -o worker/public/demo-report.html`.
- **`--score` and `--accent` are now both blues** (`#4A5CA6` vs `#14568F`). The separation that's load-bearing is score-vs-pass/fail, and that's intact — score is clearly distinct from `--no` red and `--yes` green. But if the score lane starts reading as "brand blue" rather than its own lane, that's a palette change in *both* files, so I didn't touch it unilaterally.

The palette is currently duplicated by hand across `report.css` and `index.html` with no shared source. There's a comment at the top of `report.css` saying so. Worth a real fix if they drift again.

Target reader: a program officer at a funding org who isn't technical and is wary of AI in a review process. One file plus the logs: `worker/public/index.html`.

Live preview needs a Cloudflare deploy after merge.

## Opening

The annotated specimen was the `h1`, so the page opened on raw output — which to a first-time reader parses as *us asserting these things about their proposal* rather than *this is what comes back*. Now a plain-language `h1`, a sub, a primary CTA, and the specimen demoted into a bordered `<figure>` captioned "What a finding looks like". Marking it visually as an example is what does the work.

## Ordering

Was hero → context → uploader → how-to-read → how-it-works. Now:

`why it exists → how it works → what it checks → how to read a result → uploader`

A hesitant reader reaches the upload box having already been told what happens and what comes back. Header nav and hero CTA link to `#check` so a returning user can skip it. The four-paragraph context block is trimmed to two, with the rest behind a `<details>`.

## Corrected copy that overstated the tool

This is the substantive part. Some of it was mine from the first pass, some predates it:

| Claimed | Problem | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "The checks don't use AI at all / nothing is inferred" | False — #11, #13, #14, #18 all involve a model | "Two kinds of check, kept apart": lookups a human can repeat vs. model judgements, both quote-anchored |
| "It does not judge whether AI was used" | False with Pangram (#12) as a headline feature | "An AI-detection score is a signal, not a verdict" |
| Page described a citation checker | Understates the feature set | New "What it checks" section |

For an AI-wary funder the honesty *is* the trust move — the first claim would collapse the moment they read the repo.

The new **What it checks** section covers the real feature set from the issue tree: citations #7–#11 (all four sub-checks, including "does the source support the claim it's cited for"), Pangram #12, overlap with prior submissions and reviewer pool #13/#14, tagging #15, compliance and budget #16/#17, background report #18.

**Worth flagging for reviewers:** #7–#11 aren't registered as checks yet, so an upload today returns `has_text`, `word_count`, `tagging` only. The page describes the intended feature set — per Dominique's call to use GitHub as the guide — and the honesty valve is one line under the grid noting every run reports what ran, what was skipped, and why (the repo's own degrade-to-gaps principle). Once #7–#11 land, that gap closes on its own.

## Design

Blue/green/white — the palette that reads as trustworthy, per Dominique's brief. Warm greys out: white background, blue-tinted hero band, `--panel` `#F2F7FB`, accent deepened to `#14568F` (7:1 on white), green strengthened to `#1E7A4B` with the pass lane tinted green. Red stays for failures — semantically necessary — but only on findings, never chrome.

Graphical explanation of the process, so it lands for a non-technical reader: an inline SVG `<symbol>` sprite (no network requests, `currentColor` so it themes automatically) driving a four-step process diagram for "How it works" ending on **"You decide"**, icons on the six feature cards, and ✗/✓/dial on the result lanes. Every icon is `aria-hidden` beside a real text label, so the page reads identically with images off, in a screen reader, or printed — relevant to #26.

**Drive-by fix:** buttons and chip badges hardcoded `color: #fff`, so in dark mode — where `--accent` and `--no` invert to light tints — white text sat on light fills. Added `--on-accent` / `--on-strong`.

## Deliberately not addressed

Privacy and retention. A funder's first question about uploading an applicant's document is what happens to it; #23 hasn't decided it, so I wrote nothing rather than guessing. When #23 lands, one line in the limits list is probably the highest-value addition on this page for this audience.

## Verified

Rendered at 375px, 529px, 1100px, 1200px, light and dark. All 13 `<use>` references resolve, one `h1`, no horizontal overflow at 375px, disclosure opens to the four limits and three glossary terms, upload form and its JS untouched. The wrapped-highlight `box-decoration-break` fix from #87 still holds on the narrow layouts.

Also note: `demo-report.html` is still on the old warm palette and will look like a different product beside this. Follow-up pass needed.

{"total_count":8,"incomplete_results":false,"search_type":"lexical","items":[{"id":5032828090,"number":151,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"#16: solicitation compliance checks (deterministic tier)","body":"## Summary

- Adds `slopchecker.checks.compliance`: a YAML-spec-driven solicitation compliance checker. One spec drives four checks — required-section presence, narrative length (word or page limit), budget-total-vs-ceiling, required-attachment mentions — so adding a new solicitation needs no code (issue AC #1).
- Section/attachment matching is alias-based against whatever the applicant actually wrote (e.g. "Aims" for "Specific Aims"), not the RFP's exact heading wording — same whole-word/phrase boundary matching as `checks/tagging.py`.
- Registered as `solicitation_compliance`, `tier=deterministic`, scoped to `text/markdown` via `applies_to` — this pass only detects ATX (`#`) headings, so it reports "not applicable" rather than a wrong "everything missing" result on a PDF/DOCX proposal. PDF/DOCX heading detection is follow-up work.
- No `--solicitation` given, or a value that doesn't resolve to a real YAML file, degrades to one `skipped` ledger row rather than an error. A spec dimension left unconfigured (e.g. no `required_attachments`) is simply absent from the ledger, not a gap.
- Moves `pyyaml` from the `harness`-only extra to a base dependency (the spec loader needs it at runtime).
- Two hand-compiled YAML specs (`tests/fixtures/solicitations/{aldergrove-cca,hartwell-eig}.yaml`) transcribed from the real RFPs in `fixtures/rubrics/`, tested end-to-end against their paired proposals in `harness/fixtures/`. Ground truth was hand-verified against the source RFP text, then confirmed live via the CLI — both fixtures reproduce their documented planted violations, plus one undocumented one each (missing "Data Management Plan" / missing "Evaluation Plan") found by actually reading the proposals rather than trusting the fixtures README's violation list to be exhaustive.

## Known overlap (flagged, not resolved here)

`pipeline/checks_rubric.py`'s `rubric_budget_ceiling` (#90, just landed in `debb439`) also checks budget-vs-ceiling, but via a different mechanism — it regex-parses a rubric document's raw prose for a cap phrase at runtime, no YAML spec involved. Per Emerson's own STATUS.md entry that check is an intentional stepping stone toward #16 ("next: web rubric upload slot, then spec-drafting bridge to #16"), not a competing final design. ## What's new

Grant budgets are now **itemized** (personnel / equipment / travel / indirect + a stated total). New grant-only slop defect **`budget_math`**: the stated total does not equal the sum of the line items.

- New ground-truth `budget_math` column; `_extract_budget` targets the labeled "Total requested support is $X" so `requested_budget_usd` is the stated total.
- `render_fixtures.py` adds a `budget_math` fixture (now 16 × 4 committed files).
- Corpus regenerated (126 records).

## Why it's a nice contrast

Unlike wrong-paper and near-duplicate, this one is **deterministically checkable** — sum the line items, compare to the total. `score.py` scores it with a label-aware check (robust to the sentence-shuffle in laundered docs) and the naive baseline nails it: **precision/recall 1.00**.

The corpus now tells a clean story about what a checker actually needs:

| defect | naive recall | requires |
|---|---|---|
| `has_fabricated_citations` | 1.00 | DOI resolution |
| `budget_math` | 1.00 | arithmetic |
| `missing_methods` | 1.00 | text heuristic |
| `has_mismatched_citations` | **0.00** | resolution + metadata compare |
| `is_near_duplicate` | **0.00** | corpus-wide similarity |

Deterministic checks are caught; anything needing external data or cross-document comparison is not — which is exactly the map of where the real work is.

report: adopt the #106 palette, fix badge contrast in dark mode (#74)","body":"Closes the follow-on I flagged in my own 14:02 STATUS line: #106 moved the landing page to blue/green/white while the evidence report stayed warm, so slop-checker.com and the sample report it links to read as two different products.

Confined to `src/slopchecker/report/` (mine per the ownership table) and its generated output. No `worker/src/`, no `wrangler.toml`.

## It's a value swap, not a restructure

`report.css` consumes exactly the twelve colour tokens the new palette already defines, under the same names. So this changes values in the `:root` blocks and leaves every consuming rule untouched.

## The swap alone would have hidden a real bug

`.a-id` — the annotation ID badges — hardcoded `color: #fff` against `--no` / `--yes` / `--score` / `--soft` fills. Those tokens invert to light pastels in dark mode, so it was white-on-pastel:

| dark mode | `#fff` before | `var(--on-strong)` after |
|---|---|---|
| on `--no` `#E3796F` | 2.90 | **6.26** |
| on `--yes` `#6DC194` | 2.16 | **8.41** |
| on `--score` `#9BA9EC` | 2.26 | **8.04** |
| on `--soft` `#9BABBC` | 2.35 | **7.75** |

@etbrooking — this is the same defect you fixed on the landing page in #106 ("buttons and chip badges hardcoded `#fff` over inverted light fills"). It existed identically here, and a straight palette swap would have carried it forward looking fine in light mode. Fixed the same way you did, with an `--on-strong` that flips to near-black in dark mode. Every colour in `report.css` now goes through a token — no hardcoded values left.

## Also clears both light-mode AA failures from the earlier audit

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `--soft` on `--panel` | 4.32 ❌ | **5.13** |
| `--yes` on `--panel` | 4.49 ❌ | **4.94** |

Everything else clears comfortably (`ink on bg` 15.65, `accent on bg` 7.62). `--rule` on `--bg` is 1.31, but that token is only used for dividers, which are decorative rather than UI-component boundaries — noted in the ai-log so nobody re-flags it. (#26)

## `data-theme` question is settled

The audit flagged `:root[data-theme="light"|"dark"]` as dead CSS — nothing ever set the attribute. #106 dropped those blocks from `index.html` entirely, which answers it by precedent, so they're deleted here too. Zero `data-theme` references remain in the repo.

## One copy correction

The legend read "purple = detector score". `--score` is now `#4A5CA6`, an indigo. Changed in `html.py` — leaving it would have shipped a statement that's simply false about what's on screen.

## Verification

- `demo-report.html` regenerated via `slopcheck render`, never hand-edited — and regenerated again after rebasing onto current main, byte-identical, so it isn't stale.
- Full suite: **473 passed, 1 skipped, 9 deselected**.
- Rendered and inspected in the browser at 1280px; computed `--accent` reads `#14568F`, badges render, rail intact.

## Two things worth knowing

- **Regenerating needs Python 3.11+.** This machine had only system 3.9.6, which dies on `zip(strict=True)` in the renderer. I installed `python@3.11` and made a gitignored `.venv`. Command is `slopcheck render tests/fixtures/sample_report.json -o worker/public/demo-report.html`.
- **`--score` and `--accent` are now both blues** (`#4A5CA6` vs `#14568F`). The separation that's load-bearing is score-vs-pass/fail, and that's intact — score is clearly distinct from `--no` red and `--yes` green. But if the score lane starts reading as "brand blue" rather than its own lane, that's a palette change in *both* files, so I didn't touch it unilaterally.

The palette is currently duplicated by hand across `report.css` and `index.html` with no shared source. There's a comment at the top of `report.css` saying so. Worth a real fix if they drift again.

page: reframe for funders, trust palette, process graphics (#74)","body":"Second pass on #74, driven by three rounds of feedback from Dominique. Target reader: a program officer at a funding org who isn't technical and is wary of AI in a review process. One file plus the logs: `worker/public/index.html`.

Live preview needs a Cloudflare deploy after merge.

## Opening

The annotated specimen was the `h1`, so the page opened on raw output — which to a first-time reader parses as *us asserting these things about their proposal* rather than *this is what comes back*. Now a plain-language `h1`, a sub, a primary CTA, and the specimen demoted into a bordered `<figure>` captioned "What a finding looks like". Marking it visually as an example is what does the work.

## Ordering

Was hero → context → uploader → how-to-read → how-it-works. Now:

`why it exists → how it works → what it checks → how to read a result → uploader`

A hesitant reader reaches the upload box having already been told what happens and what comes back. Header nav and hero CTA link to `#check` so a returning user can skip it. The four-paragraph context block is trimmed to two, with the rest behind a `<details>`.

## Corrected copy that overstated the tool

This is the substantive part. Some of it was mine from the first pass, some predates it:

| Claimed | Problem | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "The checks don't use AI at all / nothing is inferred" | False — #11, #13, #14, #18 all involve a model | "Two kinds of check, kept apart": lookups a human can repeat vs. model judgements, both quote-anchored |
| "It does not judge whether AI was used" | False with Pangram (#12) as a headline feature | "An AI-detection score is a signal, not a verdict" |
| Page described a citation checker | Understates the feature set | New "What it checks" section |

For an AI-wary funder the honesty *is* the trust move — the first claim would collapse the moment they read the repo.

The new **What it checks** section covers the real feature set from the issue tree: citations #7–#11 (all four sub-checks, including "does the source support the claim it's cited for"), Pangram #12, overlap with prior submissions and reviewer pool #13/#14, tagging #15, compliance and budget #16/#17, background report #18.

**Worth flagging for reviewers:** #7–#11 aren't registered as checks yet, so an upload today returns `has_text`, `word_count`, `tagging` only. The page describes the intended feature set — per Dominique's call to use GitHub as the guide — and the honesty valve is one line under the grid noting every run reports what ran, what was skipped, and why (the repo's own degrade-to-gaps principle). Once #7–#11 land, that gap closes on its own.

## Design

Blue/green/white — the palette that reads as trustworthy, per Dominique's brief. Warm greys out: white background, blue-tinted hero band, `--panel` `#F2F7FB`, accent deepened to `#14568F` (7:1 on white), green strengthened to `#1E7A4B` with the pass lane tinted green. Red stays for failures — semantically necessary — but only on findings, never chrome.

Graphical explanation of the process, so it lands for a non-technical reader: an inline SVG `<symbol>` sprite (no network requests, `currentColor` so it themes automatically) driving a four-step process diagram for "How it works" ending on **"You decide"**, icons on the six feature cards, and ✗/✓/dial on the result lanes. Every icon is `aria-hidden` beside a real text label, so the page reads identically with images off, in a screen reader, or printed — relevant to #26.

**Drive-by fix:** buttons and chip badges hardcoded `color: #fff`, so in dark mode — where `--accent` and `--no` invert to light tints — white text sat on light fills. Added `--on-accent` / `--on-strong`.

## Deliberately not addressed

Privacy and retention. A funder's first question about uploading an applicant's document is what happens to it; #23 hasn't decided it, so I wrote nothing rather than guessing. When #23 lands, one line in the limits list is probably the highest-value addition on this page for this audience.

## Verified

Rendered at 375px, 529px, 1100px, 1200px, light and dark. All 13 `<use>` references resolve, one `h1`, no horizontal overflow at 375px, disclosure opens to the four limits and three glossary terms, upload form and its JS untouched. The wrapped-highlight `box-decoration-break` fix from #87 still holds on the narrow layouts.

Also note: `demo-report.html` is still on the old warm palette and will look like a different product beside this. Follow-up pass needed.

The most immediately useful, least controversial feature. Program staff currently do this by hand on every submission, and it's entirely mechanical.

## Scope

- A solicitation spec format (YAML) capturing: required sections, page/word limits, formatting requirements (font, margins, spacing), budget ceiling, eligibility criteria, deadline, required attachments, prohibited content.
- Deterministic checks against the spec: section presence, length limits, budget total vs. ceiling, attachment presence.
- LLM-assisted checks for the judgment-dependent ones (does this address the stated priority area, does the applicant meet stated eligibility), reported as `notice` rather than `fail`.
- Optional: an LLM pass that drafts a spec YAML from a solicitation PDF, for a human to review and correct before use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One YAML spec drives the whole check; adding a new solicitation requires no code
- [ ] Deterministic and judgment-based compliance findings are visually distinct in the report
- [ ] A generated spec is always presented as a draft for human confirmation, never applied silently
- [ ] Works on a real solicitation the team can share, end to end

## Notes

Eligibility determinations have real consequences for applicants, so keep the tool advisory: it flags "page limit is 10, this appears to be 14" for a human to confirm. It never rejects anything. Worth spelling that out in the README too.

The rubric pipeline landed in #145: `CheckContext.rubric`, `slopcheck run --rubric`, and the first consumer check `rubric_budget_ceiling`. The web path is the missing leg — this issue is the whole slice, backend + frontend, so one person can ship it end-to-end.

## Backend (`src/slopchecker/web.py`)

`POST /check` gains an optional second multipart field:

```python
def check(file: UploadFile, rubric: UploadFile | None = None, format: str = "html") -> Response:
```

- When present: ingest it exactly like the submission (`ingest.ingest()` path), set the resulting `FlattenedDoc` on the context the same way the CLI does (`ctx.rubric = ...` — see `cli.py`'s `run()` for the pattern), and stamp `report.solicitation` with the rubric filename.
- When absent: nothing changes — rubric-dependent checks already emit a skipped "no rubric supplied" gap row on their own.
- Rubric fails to ingest → 422 with the ingest reason, same contract as a bad submission (surface the pipeline's own reason; don't invent one).

Note on ownership: `web.py` sits in Emerson's #27 lane — this issue is the explicit handoff of this specific change to Dominique, so no further sign-off needed. Coordinate on #27 only if you find someone else mid-edit in the file.

## Frontend (`worker/public/index.html` — your #74 lane)

- Optional "Solicitation / rubric (optional)" file input beside the proposal upload; send as the `rubric` field in the existing multipart POST.
- Copy matters: when no rubric is attached, the report will show compliance as a *coverage gap* — the UI should say so up front ("attach the RFP to check compliance; without it, compliance is reported as unchecked, not passed"). That's the we-report-our-blind-spots framing, load-bearing for the demo.
- Keep the current single-file flow working untouched when no rubric is chosen.

## Demo payoff / test material

`fixtures/rubrics/aldergrove-community-climate-rfp.md` (or the `.pdf` sibling, also in R2 `rubrics/synthetic/`) + the demo proposal → `rubric_budget_ceiling` fails with a quote-anchored finding: budget total $90,000 vs the rubric's $75,000 ceiling. Upload without the rubric → visible gap row. Both states are demo-worthy.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `POST /check` with `rubric` runs rubric checks; without it, behavior identical to today
- [ ] Bad rubric file → 422 with the pipeline's reason
- [ ] Landing page uploads both files; no-rubric state explains the coverage gap
- [ ] Verified once on slop-checker.com after Railway/Worker deploy

What a "rubric" is

Team term, settled 2026-07-31: a **rubric** is the funder-side reference document set a submission is checked against — the solicitation/RFP text, evaluation criteria and weights, program priorities, formatting and eligibility requirements. This is the thing we'd been loosely calling "reference docs."

Explicitly *not* rubrics (they already have homes):
- Cited-source texts for quote/citation verification — that's `SourceFetcher` (#10, #11).
- The prior-submission corpus for similarity — that's #14.

## Why

Three parts of the tool already assume reference material exists, and none of them define how it arrives:
- #16 (solicitation compliance) consumes a solicitation spec but has no path for the underlying document to enter the system.
- The web layer (#27) accepts exactly one upload: the submission itself.
- The CLI has no rubric argument.

## Architecture strawman

1. **Rubrics are ordinary documents.** They enter through the existing ingest layer (#4) → `FlattenedDoc`. No new parser, no special format — funders hand us PDFs.
2. **Storage:** shared and demo rubrics live in R2 under `slopchecker-docs/rubrics/` (synthetic fixtures under `rubrics/synthetic/`); the fabricated markdown sources stay in the repo at `fixtures/rubrics/`. `docs/data-storage.md` table updated as keys land. (Note: `harness/fixtures/` is deliberately NOT the home — the harness mutates and checks everything in that directory, so a rubric there would get scored as a proposal.)
3. **CLI:** `slopcheck run --rubric <path>`; later maybe an R2 key for shared rubrics.
4. **Web:** optional second multipart field `rubric` on `POST /check` — coordinated with #27, where the web layer is actively moving today.
5. **Relationship to #16:** the YAML spec is the *compiled* form of a rubric. Pipeline: rubric doc (the human artifact) → LLM-drafted spec → human review → deterministic checks. This issue owns arrival, storage, and ingest of the doc; #16 keeps the spec format and the checks themselves.
6. **Degrade to gaps:** no rubric supplied → rubric-dependent checks report coverage gaps, never crash (house rule).

## Plan

- [x] Synthetic rubric fixtures, fabricated per the #22 rule: 2–3 realistic funder docs (an RFP with formatting/budget/eligibility rules; a weighted evaluation-criteria rubric), markdown source + PDF render — landed in PR #92, `fixtures/rubrics/`
- [x] Upload to R2 `rubrics/synthetic/`, document in `docs/data-storage.md` — 6 objects, verified 2026-07-31
- [x] Verify they ingest cleanly (text layer, section structure) through `ingest.ingest()` — see PR #92; PDF loader caveat below
- [ ] `--rubric` CLI plumbing
- [ ] Web upload slot (with #27)
- [ ] Spec-drafting bridge to #16

Why

Real submissions arrive as PDFs and Word docs. Inline annotation later depends on keeping stable character offsets from the moment we extract text.

## Scope

- `slopchecker/ingest/` with one loader per format: PDF (`pymupdf`), DOCX (`python-docx`), Markdown, HTML, plain text.
- Output a `Document` with normalized text plus a structure map (page numbers for PDFs, headings for DOCX/MD) so findings can say "page 4" not just "offset 18322".
- Detect and flag documents that are image-only scans (no extractable text) rather than silently returning an empty string.
- Preserve the reference/bibliography section as an identifiable region — the citation checks need it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Round-trip test per format against fixtures in the test corpus
- [ ] `document.text[span.start:span.end]` returns the expected snippet for a known fixture
- [ ] Scanned/no-text PDF produces a clear `errored` result with an actionable message, not an empty document
- [ ] Headings/sections extracted well enough that the solicitation-compliance check can ask "is there a Methods section?"

## Notes

OCR is explicitly out of scope for the hackathon — detect and report, don't solve.
